name: ANTARES
full_name: Astronomy with a Neutrino Telescope and Abyss environmental RESearch
summary: A first-generation deep-sea neutrino telescope off Toulon that operated for sixteen years and established methods for Mediterranean neutrino astronomy before KM3NeT.
detection_principle: Photomultiplier modules on anchored flexible lines measured Cherenkov photons from relativistic particles. Timing, acoustic positioning and optical calibration supported reconstruction despite sea currents.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The collaboration explicitly reports end of data taking and full dismantling in 2022.

timeline.event: Data taking ended in February; active elements recovered by June.

collaboration.name: ANTARES Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Location
key_parameters.value: Approximately 40 km offshore Toulon in the Mediterranean Sea

results.summary: Measured atmospheric neutrinos and placed limits on astrophysical sources, diffuse fluxes and dark matter scenarios; the observatory handed over to KM3NeT.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
